primitives.name: Cap Value Regression Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model Five-stage pipeline: (1) **Stepwise OLS** of cap value (avg $/yr, cap-inflation-adjusted) on 15 candidate predictors to learn what the NFL labor market prices; exclusions: rookie contracts, non-UFAs, pre-2011-CBA contracts; duplicate-contract players averaged to one row.

primitives.assumptions: Market prices reflect true value; excludes rookie/non-UFAs; assumes linear relationship between predictors and salary.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When contract negotiations include non-performance factors or when data is sparse, regression may overfit.

layer2.mapping: Maps observed performance to market valuation; enables identification of over/underpaid players via residual analysis.

primitives.verbatim_quote: (3) **k-means** (Hartigan–Wong) on standardized salary-model predictors; k=7 chosen via **Krzanowski–Lai statistic** local maxima.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'k': 'number of clusters (k=7)', 'z_i': 'standardized predictor vector', 'c_j': 'cluster centroid j', 's(i)': 'silhouette score for player i'}
primitives.assumptions: Clusters represent homogeneous groups; intra-cluster salary variation is fair for comparison; silhouette score ensures cluster validity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When clusters are not well-separated or silhouette scores are low, anomaly detection becomes ambiguous.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that evaluating NFL linemen without film grades requires isolating individual contribution from team-level confounders. The 'differential statistics' approach achieves this by comparing performance to-side versus not-to-side, effectively controlling for teammate and RB quality. This creates a clean attribution mechanism where to-side performance reflects direct contribution. The OLS regression then maps these performance indicators to market value, capturing what the labor market prices. Clustering via k-means groups players with similar characteristics, enabling robust anomaly detection based on salary residuals within clusters. The method avoids temporal leakage by using same-season outcomes post-contract signing, ensuring the model is explanatory rather than predictive. Failure modes include poor cluster separation, which undermines anomaly detection, and overfitting due to small sample sizes or noisy predictors.
